item.title: Kubernetes pod hardening: a container is still a Linux process
item.description: Start with a quick check on one of your clusters: 1 2 kubectl run probe --rm -it --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.37 -- \ grep -E 'Seccomp:|CapEff' /proc/self/status Unless someone has already changed the defaults, you’ll see something like this: 1 2 CapEff: 00000000a80425fb Seccomp: 0 Seccomp: 0 means no syscall filter at all. The process can ask the kernel for anything its capabilities allow, and that kernel is shared with every other pod on the node.

item.title: systemd-report: a new systemd subsystem and lower-level alternative to node_exporter
item.description: systemd has a new tool called systemd-report. It gathers facts and metrics about a machine, writes them into one timestamped JSON document, optionally signs it, and can upload it to a server you choose. This is for people running fleets of servers. If you have one laptop, you’ll probably never touch it. What goes into a report There are two kinds of data.
